addendum: E (supplementary and exploratory analyses after V4)
status: LOCKED before running E1-E4. Results are reported as supplementary/exploratory; H1-H4 verdicts and the base protocol are unchanged.

common.wam: wam_coco.pth (sha256 from configs/protocol_v5_lock.json), WAM commit 2c08af04, conditions as in the base protocol (256x256, same-image multi-message, 10% checkerboard, DBSCAN eps 1 / min_samples 1000, WAM augmentation classes, 26 transforms, eligibility >= 1000 visible px)
common.statistics: image-paired percentile bootstrap, 10,000 resamples, seed 20261006, two-sided 98.75% interval; one-sided bootstrap p = (#{boot <= 0} + 1) / 10001; Holm over the 26 transforms where stated
common.data_rule: E1 and E2 read existing records only. E3 and E4 measure reserve images only (COCO val2017 indices 4500-4999, list sha256 must equal image_lists_sha256.reserve in configs/protocol_v5_lock.json). No new measurement on dev, cal or test images.

E1.question: Is BCH16 soft decoding better than BCH16 hard decoding on the test set? (secondary analysis listed in the base protocol, not computed in V4)
E1.statistic: per image: (soft successes - hard successes) / eligible messages, k = 1..5 pooled
E1.secondary_report: all 26 transforms with Holm-adjusted one-sided p
E1.document_rule: if the hflip_contrast1.5 lower bound > 0: add the interval to the abstract sentence 'hard 복호보다도 높았다(0.944 대 0.891)'. Otherwise delete that sentence from the abstract and write 'soft 복호의 추가 이득은 시험에서 확인되지 않았다' in 5.8 and 7.

E2.question: Does C still beat A at the same calibrated false-attribution level when near-miss unregistered messages are not part of the threat model?
E2.procedure: for methods A, B_margin, C_max: per scene null score = max over sources excluding 'unreg_near' (-inf if none); threshold on cal with the locked rule (accept s iff (1 + #{cal null >= s}) / 1001 <= 0.002, i.e. s > second-largest cal null); apply to test with the same exclusion
E2.report: per method: threshold (and t for A), false attributions / 3,000, one-sided Clopper-Pearson upper bound at 98.75%, R; R(C) - R(A) and R(C) - R(B) with 98.75% interval over images with at least one registered eligible message
E2.approximation: near-miss messages remain embedded in the scenes; only their units' scores are excluded from the null scores
E2.document_rule: add as 'threat-model sensitivity' under 4.4 and table 3 of 5.8. If the R(C) - R(A) lower bound <= 0, state in the abstract and section 6 that the H2 advantage holds under the threat model with near-miss unregistered messages.

E3.question: Is BCH16 soft better than a message of the same 16-bit capacity without coding redundancy?

seeds.transforms: stable_seed(20261103, 'v5-reserve-e3', k, batch_start, transform), batches of 25 in index order

message_sets.REP16: 16 information bits repeated twice, random IDs
message_sets.PAD16: bits 0-15 = random 16-bit ID, bits 16-31 = one fixed 16-bit key drawn from the pad_key seed, identical for all messages

decoders.PAD16 hard: DBSCAN centroid bits 0-15 equal the ID
decoders.PAD16 soft: signs of the region's mean logits at bits 0-15 equal the ID (maximum likelihood over the PAD16 codebook, since bits 16-31 are constant)

E3.primary_exploratory: hflip_contrast1.5: per-image BCH16 soft - PAD16 soft, 98.75% interval
E3.secondary: all 26 transforms (Holm); BCH16 soft - PAD16 hard; PAD16 soft - RAW; BCH16 soft - RAW for comparison with the test result
E3.document_rule: if the primary lower bound > 0: add to the abstract and section 6 (H1) that BCH16 soft is also higher than a message of the same 16-bit capacity without coding. Otherwise explain the H1 gain as capacity reduction plus soft decoding and do not claim an additional gain from coding redundancy.

E4.question: What does each stage cost?
E4.data: the first 100 reserve images; transforms none and hflip_contrast1.5; k = 5; BCH16 and PAD16 messages; wam_coco
E4.timing: per image: WAM.embed (one message), WAM.detect, DBSCAN (GPU implementation), BCH16 soft decoding (all regions, 65,536 x 32 correlation per region), BCH16 hard decoding, PAD16 decoding; torch.cuda.synchronize around every stage; the first 10 images are warm-up and excluded
E4.report: median and 95th percentile in ms per stage, GPU name, batch size 1
E4.document_rule: fill table 6 of section 5.8 with these values
